crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: AI and Authorship
children.blurb: AI and authorship concerns who or what counts as an author when generative models contribute to text, code, images, or research outputs.

children.name: Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking
children.blurb: Fabricated citations are references that look real but do not correspond to any published work, often produced when a language model generates a plausible but nonexistent paper title, author list, or DOI.

children.name: Training Data and Academic Work
children.blurb: Training data and academic work covers the use of scholarly texts, including journal articles, preprints, theses, and course materials, as inputs for machine learning systems.

children.name: Ethics Review with AI Assistance
children.blurb: Ethics review with AI assistance covers the use of machine learning and natural language tools to support institutional review boards, research ethics committees, and journal editors in screening protocols, identifying risks, checking consent language, and flagging conflicts or missing safeguards.

children.name: Provenance of Research Images and Data
children.blurb: Provenance of research images and data is the record of where a dataset or image came from, how it was created or collected, who modified it, and under what conditions it can be reused.

sections.body: This field covers how artificial intelligence is used and misused in the production and checking of scholarly work. Right now AI systems write drafts, suggest author lists, generate citations, and create or alter research images. They also check manuscripts for factual errors, compare claims against sources, and trace where training data came from. The work is not theoretical, it is happening in manuscript preparation, peer review, and data management. The pages under this section describe those specific uses and the integrity problems they create.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work stands unevenly. Authorship detection and fabricated citation checking are partially solved for obvious cases, but subtle AI generated text and plausible fake references still slip through. Training data provenance is far from solved, because many models do not disclose their sources and academic work can be ingested without consent. Ethics review with AI assistance is early and inconsistent, and provenance of research images and data remains a hard problem, especially with generative edits. The site's library holds 135 research papers and 11,075 extracted claims, which shows the volume of evidence but not a settled answer. Honest limits include unreliable detection tools, missing provenance records, and the fact that no automated system can replace human judgment about authorship or ethics.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking at who gets credit should start with AI and Authorship, which explains how tools affect author lists and contribution. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking covers the specific failure of made up references and the tools that try to catch them. Training Data and Academic Work connects model training to scholarly sources and the consent questions that follow. Ethics Review with AI Assistance shows where AI is being tried in review boards and what it can and cannot do. Provenance of Research Images and Data closes the loop by tracing how visual and numerical evidence is created, altered, and verified. Together they move from the person, to the citation, to the data, to the review, and finally to the evidence itself.
